**Refined prompt:** Trace the comment author through the POST/GET comment path and name the exact line(s) where it's lost — diagnosis from the code, cited file:line, no fix applied yet.

## Short answer

You don't lose it. It's never captured, and there's nowhere to put it if you did.

`author` is absent at all four layers of the comment path. The deepest one is the schema, so the other three can't be fixed independently.

## The trace

**1. Controller — the caller's identity is never read.** `src/article/article.controller.ts:77`

```ts
async createComment(@Param('slug') slug, @Body('comment') commentData: CreateCommentDto) {
```

No `@User('id')` parameter. Compare `create()` two handlers up at `article.controller.ts:52`, which does take `@User('id') userId: number` and passes it through.

The identity *is* available here — `POST articles/:slug/comments` is in the `AuthMiddleware` list at `article.module.ts:28`, so the request is authenticated and `req.user` is populated. The handler just never asks for it. This is the first drop, and it's a pure omission.

**2. DTO — no field to carry it.** `src/article/dto/create-comment.ts:1-3` declares only `body`. (Per LESSONS.md #112 this wouldn't *strip* an author at runtime — but nothing is sending one.)

**3. Service — only `body` is set.** `src/article/article.service.ts:104-105`

```ts
const comment = new Comment();
comment.body = commentData.body;
```

Then `article.comments.push(comment)` and save. The comment is persisted with a body and an `articleId`, nothing else.

**4. Entity — there is no author column.** `src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15` has exactly three members: `id`, `body`, and `@ManyToOne article`. No `@ManyToOne(() => UserEntity)`, no `authorId` FK. This is the root cause — even if you fixed layers 1–3 today, `comment.author` has no column to land in.

## Where it's *not* lost

Worth ruling out, since the symptom looks like a serialization bug:

- **The read path is innocent.** `findComments()` (`article.service.ts:165-168`) returns `article.comments` straight off the eager relation (`article.entity.ts:40`), untransformed. No mapper is dropping the field.
- **The `Comment` interface at `article.interface.ts:3-5` declares only `body`** — but that's a TypeScript interface, and interfaces don't filter at runtime. If the entity had an author, it would serialize out despite this type. It documents the gap; it doesn't cause it.

So: the API is returning exactly what's in the database, and the database has no author.

## One adjacent bug you'll hit right after

`addComment()` returns `Promise<ArticleRO>` — `{article}` — at `article.service.ts:111`. The RealWorld spec returns `{comment}` from `POST /articles/:slug/comments`. Your frontend reading `response.comment.author` will get `undefined` on the property *before* it ever gets to `author`. Same shape as LESSONS.md #57.

## Scope note

This is item 2 on `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12`, which flags it as design-first precisely because of the missing relation. A fix touches the entity (new `@ManyToOne` author + eager or explicit `relations`), `synchronize: true` regenerating the table (`schema.md:6-9` — no migrations here), the service write path, the controller signature, and the `CommentsRO` type. It also unblocks the ownership check on `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id`, which `auth.md:60` notes is currently impossible — "comments have no author to compare against anyway."

Want me to draft that change? I'd propose the entity + write path first, since the response-shape work depends on it.

**Not read:** `src/user/auth.middleware.ts` and `src/user/user.decorator.ts` — my claim that `req.user` is populated on this route rests on `article.module.ts:28` (which I read) plus `.claude/knowledge/auth.md:19-26` (which I did not verify against source). `prisma/` ignored per `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22-24`.
